solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Run back, getting angry, though not at first at an intense level

indicators.note: back tells us the verb for running fast is written in reverse order

parts.note: to run fast is to speed

indicators.note: though not at first says the word for angry loses its opening letter

parts.note: heated means angry

explanation.surface: Someone sprints back, furious, though at first not very intensely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SPEED into DEEPS; 'though not at first' drops the H of HEATED, leaving EATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deep-rooted operates at a profound, intense level, the adjective's sense of firmly embedded feeling.

clue.text: Fool to try gym at school

parts.note: a do is an attempt, a try
PE, physical education, is the school gym lesson

explanation.surface: A clumsy pupil has a go at gymnastics in school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is only a link, and 'do' here is the noun for an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: a dope is a stupid person, an idiot.

clue.text: Former airman deferring current adventure

indicators.note: deferring means putting off till later, so one letter is moved further along

parts.note: ex- means former
a pilot is an airman
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: An ex-RAF pilot postpones an electrically charged escapade.
explanation.walkthrough: EX PILOT with its I 'deferred' (moved later) gives EXPLOIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an exploit is a daring deed or adventurous feat.

clue.text: I pledge to fill train, providing illumination

indicators.note: to fill means going inside the word for a train or series

parts.note: a string is a train or series of things
to plight is to pledge, as in plighting one's troth

explanation.surface: A promise to supply a train with lamps, so it is lit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to fill' puts the pledge inside the train, split around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Strip lighting means fluorescent tubes, a form of illumination.

clue.text: Almost certain to replace one of first four letters? Ridiculous

indicators.note: to replace one of says a letter of the alphabet's opening run is swapped out

parts.note: the alphabet starts A, B, C, D

indicators.note: almost means the word for certain is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about swapping a letter, judged ridiculous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims SURE to SUR, which takes the place of C in ABCD.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: absurd things are laughably unreasonable, ridiculous.

clue.text: Love our family, say, engaged in error, turning up for adoption

indicators.note: engaged in means held inside the other word
turning up, in a down answer, means the word for error is read bottom to top

parts.note: a lapse is a slip or error
love is zero, O, in tennis
a family might call itself us

explanation.surface: A family in love with itself makes a mistake about adopting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses the error word first (ESPAL); 'engaged in' then puts love and family inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Espousal is the embracing or taking up of a cause, its adoption.

clue.text: Part of orchestra obscuring entry of ropey singer

indicators.note: obscuring means hiding, so that letter vanishes from the section name

parts.note: the brass is a section of an orchestra

indicators.note: entry of means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A section of the orchestra drowns out a poor vocalist's entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obscuring' removes R, the entry of 'ropey', from BRASS.
explanation.definitionFit: A bass is a singer with the lowest male voice.

clue.text: A doubter, dismissing second item with germicidal properties

indicators.note: dismissing second item means the second letter of the word for a doubter is dropped

parts.note: a sceptic doubts things

explanation.surface: A doubter rejects a second thing claimed to kill germs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second item' is the second letter, C, of SCEPTIC, not S for second.
explanation.definitionFit: Aseptic means free from germs, so it describes things that sterilise or disinfect.

clue.text: Startled cry sparks energy to enter building

indicators.note: to enter means going into the shuffled letters
startled suggests the letters jumping about into a new order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A frightened shout as sparks fly when power reaches a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Startled' rearranges CRY SPARKS; E goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a skyscraper is a very tall building.

clue.text: Suffer endless scramble to secure page in historic paper

indicators.note: to secure means holding the next letter inside

parts.note: to pay is to suffer for something

indicators.note: endless says the final letter of the word for scramble is cut

parts.note: a rush is a scramble

explanation.surface: Endless hurry and suffering in old paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims RUSH to RUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Papyrus was the writing material of ancient Egypt, so a historic kind of paper.

clue.text: Captured soldier, deprived of drink, retaining little energy — liable to crumble?

parts.note: a POW is a prisoner of war

indicators.note: retaining means keeping the next letter inside

parts.note: dry means without drink, or alcohol
E is the short form of energy

explanation.surface: A prisoner of war, thirsty and drained of strength, is near collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a slightly loose definition: powdery things crumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Powdery things are made of fine grains and fall apart easily.

clue.text: Help athlete win when running, avoiding one learner's impediment

indicators.note: running suggests letters moving about into a new order
avoiding means one letter is left out of the fodder

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a learner driver

explanation.surface: Coaching an athlete to victory, with a novice getting in the way.
explanation.walkthrough: HELP ATHLETE WIN has two Ls; 'avoiding' takes one out before 'when running' shuffles the rest. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A white elephant is a burdensome possession, a costly hindrance or impediment.

clue.text: Left University after work? Mostly stay, seizing the moment

indicators.note: after places the next pieces behind the short word for work

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
port is the nautical word for left

indicators.note: mostly says the last letter of the word for stay is removed

parts.note: to stick is to stay put

explanation.surface: Someone leaves college after a job, mostly staying to make the most of their chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' cuts STICK to STIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Opportunistic behaviour exploits openings as they arise, grabbing chances.

clue.text: Unmoved cash register company does it

parts.note: what a firm does to its register is stock it, with 'it' standing for the till
a till is a cash register

explanation.surface: A cash register firm is unmoved by events.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay as 'a company stocks till': split the answer 6,4.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock-still means completely motionless, utterly unmoved.

clue.text: Bird accepted bait (small piece of food)

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
a fish that bit has taken the bait

explanation.surface: A little bird snapped up the bait, a tasty morsel.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a titbit is a tasty morsel.

clue.text: Mediterranean port, Nice, unfortunately swamped by molten lava

indicators.note: swamped by means surrounded by the other letters
molten suggests letters melted into a new arrangement
unfortunately suggests things going wrong, here the letters' order

explanation.surface: A French Riviera town sadly engulfed by flowing lava.
explanation.walkthrough: 'molten' makes VALA and 'unfortunately' makes ENCI, which 'swamped by' places inside. Nice is a French Riviera city.
explanation.definitionFit: Valencia is a Spanish city with a harbour on the Mediterranean.

clue.text: About to be nipped by beetle, say, where you wouldn't want people to see?

definitions.text: where you wouldn't want people to see?

indicators.note: to be nipped by means held between the jaws of the other word

parts.note: a beetle is an example of an insect
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Being bitten by a bug somewhere private you'd rather not show.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something privately, hidden from others, is the adverbial idiom's sense.

clue.text: Mobile communicator to get sharper after quibble

indicators.note: after places the sharpening word behind the quibbling word

parts.note: to carp is to quibble or nitpick
to hone is to sharpen

explanation.surface: A phone that gets smarter after people grumble about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A car phone was an early in-vehicle telephone, a mobile device.

clue.text: Egyptian city went down in list

indicators.note: in places the setting word inside the list

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties
the sun set, went down

explanation.surface: An Egyptian city drops down a table of rankings.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosetta is a port city in the Nile Delta, home of the famous Stone.

clue.text: Mountain's gone over by half of visitors, causing bother

indicators.note: gone over means turned back to front

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain; the 's is 'has'

indicators.note: half of means the opening three of six letters

parts.note: guests are visitors

explanation.surface: Tourists swarming over a mountain are a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone over' turns ALP into PLA; 'half of' takes GUE from GUESTS. 'causing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to plague someone is to pester or harass them.

clue.text: Miss one thing studied by astrologer or astronomer

parts.note: a gal is a girl, a miss
I is the Roman numeral one
Leo is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A girl skips something an astrologer or stargazer would study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a verb, but it is a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Galileo Galilei was the Italian astronomer who championed the telescope.

clue.text: Hesitant about a couple of books in poor condition

indicators.note: about means surrounding the letters that follow

parts.note: shy means hesitant or wary
B is book, so two books is BB

explanation.surface: Someone timid about a pair of tatty old books.
explanation.definitionFit: Shabby things are worn and threadbare, in poor repair.

clue.text: Painter's masterpiece, else his paint misplaced around ceiling, primarily

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters surround the next letter
misplaced means the letters are put in the wrong places
primarily means just the first letter

explanation.surface: A painter's great work, or else his paint went astray on the ceiling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misplaced' rearranges ELSE HIS PAINT around C, the first letter of 'ceiling'.
explanation.definitionFit: Michelangelo's Sistine Chapel ceiling is a painter's masterpiece.

clue.text: Kind City people will suppress it

indicators.note: will suppress it says the answer is held down inside the phrase, unseen

explanation.surface: Kind folk in the City will keep quiet about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a type is a kind or sort.

clue.text: Figure, say, included by artist omitting old man

indicators.note: included by means placed inside the other word
omitting means leaving out the next piece

parts.note: a painter is an artist
pa is father, one's old man
say means for example, eg

explanation.surface: A figure, for instance, appears in a painting by an artist without a father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure, say' looks like one phrase, but 'say' is EG. PAINTER without PA is INTER.
explanation.definitionFit: An integer is a whole number, a figure.

clue.text: Laugh coarsely about the setter eating large apple

indicators.note: about means wrapped around the remaining letters

parts.note: to bray is to laugh loudly like a donkey

indicators.note: eating means taking in the next letter

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: Someone guffaws at the setter munching a big apple.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Bramley is a British cooking apple.

clue.text: Centrepiece of release by maverick ultimately is disclosure

indicators.note: centrepiece of means the central letters of the word
ultimately means the final letter

explanation.surface: A maverick's press release turns out to be a leak.
explanation.walkthrough: The centre of RELEASE gives LEA; add K from 'maverick'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a leak is an unauthorised disclosure of information.

clue.text: Put off by a book about holidays, initially unwilling to travel

parts.note: to stay a judgment is to postpone it

indicators.note: about means surrounding the next letter

parts.note: a tome is a large book

indicators.note: initially means just the first letter

explanation.surface: Delayed by a book on holidays, someone decides not to travel.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay-at-home person prefers to remain at home, reluctant to go anywhere.
